chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Bakr al-Farisi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated from Hammad, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who stays awake during the night of Eid, his heart will not die on the day the hearts die.'

key_terms.يَوْمَ تَمُوتُ الْقُلُوبُ: The day the hearts die (Day of Judgment/Resurrection)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of staying awake on the night of Eid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the spiritual vitality achieved through night-long devotion on Eid, contrasting the believer's living heart with those that perish in heedlessness. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *Ihya al-Layl* (reviving the night) as a means to preserve spiritual consciousness against the collective forgetfulness of the Day of Judgment.
